review_notes: I read the whole file. It has almost no simp attributes, and most declarations are one-off proof steps. I checked the definitions behind the two candidate interfaces: `unitF`, and the `centralScalar_apply_*` and `archComponent_*` lemmas in the Definitions files. I did not search for other users of `unitF`; the long grep for `unitF` and related names returned only a broad file list. I did not run Lean, so both suggestions are untested. They are modest and concern coverage and usability, not loops or competing rules. I did not recommend simp attributes for `norm_ofRealAt` or the primed norm lemmas, because they are only used via targeted `rw`.

findings.excerpt: theorem unitF_val (ε : (𝓞 F)ˣ) : ((unitF F ε : Fˣ) : F) = ((ε : 𝓞 F) : F) := rfl
findings.problem: `unitF` is a new def that wraps `Units.map`. Its only coercion lemma `unitF_val` is not tagged `@[simp]`, and there is no matching lemma for the inverse. Callers therefore work around the gap. Line 64 unfolds the definition with `simp [unitF]`, so the goal is exposed to `Units.map` internals. Line 326 passes `unitF_val` to `simp` by hand. Unfolding the def is the wrong normal form, because `↑(unitF F ε)` should reduce to `((ε : 𝓞 F) : F)`. The inverse case (`↑(unitF F ε)⁻¹`) has no canonical rewrite at all.
findings.proposed_change: Mark `unitF_val` with `@[simp]`. Add a companion `@[simp] unitF_inv_val : ((unitF F ε)⁻¹ : Fˣ) = (((ε⁻¹ : (𝓞 F)ˣ) : 𝓞 F) : F)`. Both can be proved by `rfl` or `Units.coe_map_inv`. Then replace `simp [unitF]` on line 64 and `simp [..., unitF_val]` on line 326 with plain `simp`. The definition can then be kept irreducible to `simp`.
findings.benefit: The `diagOne (unitF F ε)` matrix entries reduce to the integral entries of `ε` directly. Callers no longer unfold `unitF` or list `unitF_val` by hand.

findings.excerpt: theorem archComponent_centralScalar_archIdele (w : InfinitePlace F) (a : ∀ w : InfinitePlace F, (w.Completion)ˣ) :
findings.problem: The four matrix entries of the archimedean component of `centralScalar (archIdele a)` are packed into one four-way conjunction, so `simp` and `rw` cannot use them as rewrite rules. Each conjunct repeats a long left-hand side. The proof applies `centralScalar_apply_eq` or `centralScalar_apply_ne` and then closes with `rfl`. The use site has to destructure the result with `obtain ⟨hZ00, hZ01, hZ10, hZ11⟩`, and it then needs `rw [← hz'] at` to repair the form. The underlying `glFin_centralScalar_archIdele` also has no simp attribute, although it is only used in a `rw` chain that ends in `one_mul`.
findings.proposed_change: Split the lemma into separate entry equations: one for the diagonal, `(archComponent ... (glArch ... (centralScalar ... (archIdele F a))) : Matrix ...) i i = a w`, and one for the off-diagonal case `i ≠ j`, which gives `0`. These mirror the existing `centralScalar_apply_eq` and `centralScalar_apply_ne`. Tag the diagonal and off-diagonal versions `@[simp]`, and tag `glFin_centralScalar_archIdele` `@[simp]` as well. The `hZ00 … hZ11` arguments to `step_place` can then be discharged with `by simp` in the same way as the `hU` hypotheses on lines 481–489.
findings.benefit: The entries of `centralScalar (archIdele a)` become part of the simp normal form. Call sites can use `simp` or `rw` instead of destructuring a conjunction. The statements are also shorter.
